sendTest: Microsoft built an AI that hunts for security holes and says it beats OpenAI's and Anthropic's best, at half the cost.
centralClaim: Microsoft launched its first cybersecurity AI model, MAI-Cyber-1-Flash, built to find vulnerabilities in complex codebases, alongside an agentic security system called Perception.

corroboration.quote: Microsoft on Monday launched its first cybersecurity-specialized model alongside a new AI cybersecurity platform at a small event in San Francisco, taking a big swipe at major players in the space - namely Anthropic, Google, and OpenAI.
Microsoft has introduced MAI-Cyber-1-Flash, a security-focused AI model built into MDASH , the company's multi-agent vulnerability identification and remediation system.

caption:
Microsoft wants to be the one guarding your company's software, at half the price.

On Monday it launched MAI-Cyber-1-Flash, its first AI model built only for security work. Inside MDASH, Microsoft's system for finding and fixing software flaws, the model scored 96% on a test of finding real vulnerabilities in code, 12 points above Anthropic's Mythos. Microsoft says the combination delivers world-class performance at 50% of the cost of leading models.

It also launched Perception, a set of AI agents that monitor, patch and simulate attacks continuously. Microsoft's security vice president Hayete Gallot framed it plainly: defend against AI with AI, because the attackers already use it.

The caveat, plainly: every score is Microsoft's own reporting, published in its own announcement. An outside party assessed the model before release; the numbers are still the company's.

Would you let one company both write your software and grade its own security? Say it in the comments.
